subject: Security questionnaire initiation — clarifying KMS, encryption-in-transit, and SOC 2 timing
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex@fintegral.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + security questionnaire preference

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency numbers looked promising and the team is excited to continue the evaluation. Security is the next gating item for procurement.

A few quick items from our side as we get the questionnaire started:
- We can provide a CAIQ (Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire) or our own custom form — which do you prefer?
- We completed a SOC 2 Type II in April 2025; attaching the PDF for reference.
- Can you confirm what level of encryption detail you need (KMS integration + key ownership vs. standard at-rest encryption)? We use customer-managed KMS for a subset of enterprise customers but would like to know what Redwood requires to proceed.
- We are not handling PHI today, but we do process hashed PII for tokenization flows. GDPR considerations apply; would you need additional DPIA info?

Attaching: SOC2-Full-Report-2025.pdf, network-diagram.png (high level)

Alex Li
Head of Cloud Security, Fintegral
alex@fintegral.com
[Attachment: SOC2-Full-Report-2025.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)]
[Attachment: network-diagram.png (PNG, 450KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@fintegral.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + security questionnaire preference

Hi Alex — great to meet you earlier, and thanks for sending the SOC 2 doc and diagram.

Short answers up front: we prefer the CAIQ/ SIG format for initial scoping (it maps cleanly to our evidence catalog). If there are specific controls in your custom form you want prioritized, we can consume both, but CAIQ is faster for us to process.

A few clarifying questions so we can route to the right owners and build a realistic timeline:
1) Data types: you mentioned hashed PII — can you list exact attributes you expect to send (emails hashed, user_id, device fingerprints, etc.)?
2) Residency: do you need data to be stored in a specific region (US-only) for this evaluation?
3) KMS: when you say "customer-managed KMS for a subset of customers," do you mean you can expose a key management API we can call, or you use a separate key per tenant in your cloud account?
4) SOC 2: good to see Type II — is there an expiration date / next audit window we should note?
5) Regulatory: you indicated GDPR applies; please confirm whether you expect Redwood to act as a data processor only, and whether a standard DPA will suffice.

Our proposed next steps:
- We will run CAIQ prefilling items that are straightforward and send an evidence request list (ETA 3 business days).
- If you need a BAA or have special HIPAA needs later, flag it now so legal can triage.

Looping in Jordan (platform security) and Karthik (sales engineering) to weigh in on KMS and evidence requirements.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Security Manager, Redwood Inference
monica@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: Redwood-CAIQ-prefill-template.xlsx (CSV stub)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up + security questionnaire preference

Monica / Karthik — quick note after skimming their attachments:

- SOC 2 looks current (Type II covering Apr 2025 window). We should validate scope (production vs. non-prod).
- Network diagram is high level; ask for a brief listing of ingress/egress IPs and any third-party providers (CDN, object store).
- On KMS: our preferred flow is one of these two options — (A) tenant-specific CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) where we can integrate via a key-wrapping API, or (B) use your tenant-specific key stored in your cloud account and provide attestations. Option A is heavier but aligns with enterprise compliance.

Karthik — can you confirm estimated effort to validate TLS versions and key-wrapping support? If we can get a SKU/quote note for Dedicated customers who require CMEK, include that in the reply.

Jordan
Principal Security Engineer
[internal note: prefer CAIQ for initial pass; custom form later if they insist]

From: Alex Li <alex@fintegral.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@fintegral.com
Date: 2027-06-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + security questionnaire preference

Hi all — thanks for the fast response. Quick answers inline: 
- Data types: currently we send hashed emails (sha256), user_id (UUID), and basic device metadata (browser, IP). No PHI for this pilot.
- Residency: US-only storage is preferred for the initial pilot.
- KMS: we support option B today (tenant-specific key stored in our cloud account per customer). We can discuss a roadmap to CMEK (option A) for later phases; engineering estimates ~6–8 weeks to support key-wrapping APIs.
- SOC2: report covers controls through 2025-04-30; next audit window is Q2 2028.
- DPA: we are happy to sign your standard DPA and will confirm processor/ controller roles — security@fintegral.com copied.

We prefer CAIQ to start. Attaching the same SOC 2 PDF and our internal CAIQ export (CSV) for you to ingest.

Next steps we propose:
1) Monica & team to send prefilled CAIQ items/ evidence checklist (you mentioned ~3 business days).
2) We'll assemble ingress/egress IPs and the list of third-party providers by EOD Tuesday.
3) If CMEK is required for procurement, we can open a roadmap ticket and discuss Dedicated/reserved capacity options with your sales engineering team.

Alex Li
Head of Cloud Security, Fintegral
alex@fintegral.com
[Attachment: Fintegral-CAIQ-export.csv (CSV, 120KB)]
